inputs.original_text: A parent of three children in South Portland’s public schools is apologizing to the educators and staff facing another budget shortfall and cuts of more than 70 positions. This is not just a line in a budget: it means putting more pressure on school workers and risking support for students. Public education should not be forced to absorb the consequences of chronic underinvestment. The people who keep schools running—and the children who depend on them—deserve better.
inputs.modified_text: A South Portland parent of three is apologizing to school staff as they face another budget shortfall and cuts of more than 70 positions. That shouldn’t be treated as an unavoidable accounting problem: when public schools are chronically underfunded, workers are made to carry the strain and students risk losing the support they need. Educators and school staff deserve decent conditions, and children shouldn’t pay the price for institutions failing to invest in them.
